Hey Jasmine — thanks for flagging. This is a recurring DST edge case between Calendly and some browsers when the attendee's OS timezone is different from the browser locale. Short checklist/workarounds that work for customers:

1) Chili Piper redirect: use the timezone param in the redirect URL so the scheduling page renders with Europe/Berlin. Example: https://chilpiper.com/redirect/demo-acme?tz=Europe%252FBerlin — we've had good success with that for EU prospects.

2) Manual ICS + explicit TZ: send a manual invite (ICS) that sets the DTSTART/DTEND with the TZID=Europe/Berlin. That ensures Outlook/Google parse correctly even if Calendly misreported.

3) Calendly URL param: append ?tz=Europe%252FBerlin to force the presentation timezone, but note this doesn't fix invites created by some browser time settings.

4) Copy the UTC time in the invite body the way we do for cross-region demos (e.g., "Tue May 5, 14:00 CET / 12:00 UTC / 06:00 PT"). That reduces confusion when people look at different calendar apps.

For now I suggest sending the Chili Piper link with tz param + an ICS as backup. I'll paste a ready Chili Piper link below you can drop into the email.

Chili Piper link (EU forced): https://chilpiper.com/redirect/demo-acme?tz=Europe%252FBerlin

If you want, I can also create and attach an ICS for Tue May 5, 15:00 CET and drop it in the thread.

— Camila
